slot.brief: letter pair analogy where each letter shifts by a fixed positional value; ask for the analogous pair among options, with a mixed-letters distractor

stem: Complete the analogy in the same manner: BK : GP :: NI : ?

verdicts.working: B→G and K→P are both shifts of +5. Applying the same shifts: N→S and I→N, giving SN.
issues: The option images appear unrelated to the letter analogy; options A and B show identical diagrams, despite having different text answers.

working:
Rule: each letter advances 5 places. BK -> GP: B(2)+5=G(7), K(11)+5=P(16). Apply to NI: N(14)+5=S(19), I(9)+5=N(14) => SN. (A) NS reverses the order. (C) SS changes I to S (+10). (D) CN changes N to C (no +5).

Independent check: B→G and K→P are both shifts of +5. Applying the same shifts: N→S and I→N, giving SN.
solution: Each letter advances $5$ places in the alphabet: $B\to G$ and $K\to P$. Thus, $N\to S$ and $I\to N$, giving $\boxed{SN}$.
